why: The other page shape of the same site, and the reason a body rule says what a page is rather than only where its prose sits. A listing whose entries carry the opening paragraph of each post is several hundred words of genuine prose, so the sliver rule keeps it and the archive gains a listing filed beside the articles. The rule that names the post's own element answers this page too, because a page that does not have one is not a post. What this case pins is the answer and not the selector: any body selector absent from this page produces it, and the topic page the selector was written against is deliberately not in the corpus, for the reason in docs/readability.md. So a green suite here is not evidence that div.topic-full-text is where that site puts its posts.
title: Topics in ~comp

rules.why: a topic page nests the replies inside the same element as the post, so the post has to be named directly
